rule: Flagged items do not block publication. Each states what is wrong, what it affects, and the observation that would close it.

rows.finding: The twelve legacbacktest rules were defined after their scoring data existed. Their published ROI figures are selection-exposed: twelve hypotheses were searched in one run.
rows.affects: Every ROI and win-rate number in data/s9cb/leaderboard.json
rows.mitigation: Registered as registered-backtest with the exposure stated; the multiplicity charge in the leaderboard pays for the search; no legacy rule can be promoted.

rows.finding: No opening price exists anywhere in the repository, and the closing price carries no fetch time. The price-snapshot store the brief requires is therefore blocked by a data-source decision, not by engineering.
rows.resolved: Open — needs a decision from the owner
rows.mitigation: Q02 and W11 state the exact observation that would clear it.

rows.finding: S11 and S12 read an injury-designation level from the weekly report. The brief explicitly forbids a level as a signal and asks for a surprise instead.
rows.mitigation: Both stay scored so the comparison is visible; the surprise rules P07-P09 replace them and the level rules can never be promoted.

rows.finding: The historical results and closing lines are a third-party (nflverse) extract of the NFL GSIS feed. The repository's official check covers the 2026 season only, so the historical intervals rest on an unverified transcription.
rows.mitigation: Q03 names the reconciliation that would close it.

rows.finding: The model loses to the closing line on all three markets (side -0.0413, total -0.0346, moneyline -0.0714).
rows.affects: The origination claim the project is built on
rows.mitigation: Stated on the overview and in the executive summary. W01-W03 record what would reverse it.

rows.finding: No player-prop price exists in the repository, so three of six leaderboard divisions cannot be scored at all.
rows.mitigation: Q10; the divisions are published as blank with the reason rather than omitted.

rows.finding: The two-estimator comparison has no winner: the holdout paired difference is -0.0136 points with an interval of -0.2288 to +0.2188.
rows.affects: Any claim that the rating model adds information on the total
rows.mitigation: Both estimators published until one wins (W05).

rows.finding: The promotion rule is not pre-registered, so the competition has a pre-registered exit and no pre-registered entrance.
2,072 table rows with official source links are published row-level while the licence question in flag F51 is unresolved.
rows.resolved: Open — carried from F51, not re-litigated here

rows.finding: The third-party extract holds a completed Week 10 game (WAS 24, NYG 21) that the repository's own official transcription file did not contain; the gap is now closed by an official Game Center row fetched in this build.
rows.affects: The 2026 results corpus; reconciles with the earlier session's flag F49
rows.mitigation: Official rows 137, matched 137, mismatched 0. The reconciliation is published game by game on the Official Reconciliation page and runs as a build step.

rows.finding: The reconciliation covers 137 rows of 2026 only. The other seasons behind the leaderboard's intervals are unverified against any official page.
rows.mitigation: Q03 and readiness row PR-02 name the extension route: official Game Books, season by season.

rows.finding: The default figure for the strategy family's multiplicity charge assumes the twelve rules are independent tests. Several share inputs (S01/S02, S03/S04), so the charge is conservative in the wrong direction.
rows.affects: The multiplicity column on the leaderboard
